title: Longest Unequal Adjacent Groups Subsequence I
summary: Given a string array words and a binary array groups of equal length, find the longest subsequence of words where the corresponding elements in groups are alternating (i.e., no two consecutive elements are the same).
statement: Given a string array words and a binary array groups of equal length, find the longest subsequence of words where the corresponding elements in groups are alternating (i.e., no two consecutive elements are the same). Return any valid longest alternating subsequence. Note that all elements in words are unique.
constraints: words and groups have the same length, and each group is zero or one.
Choose a longest subsequence whose adjacent chosen entries have different groups.
Return the chosen words in original order; any longest answer is allowed, and this function returns the earliest greedy answer.
hints: Within a run of equal group values, at most one word can be chosen.
Choose the first word of every maximal equal-group run.
Append exactly when the group differs from the last chosen group.
This takes one word per run, which is feasible and also matches the upper bound, so it is longest.
editorial: This takes one word per run, which is feasible and also matches the upper bound, so it is longest.

The first three words alternate groups; the final group repeats one.
